system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Scope note:** I've reviewed the Seller's summary update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). I haven't seen the full Seller SPA text, so clause references are taken from the Seller's summary and should be checked against the actual draft. The Seller calls these "key negotiated positions" and says the package is "fair and balanced." Under playbook §6.3, that label doesn't make any term agreed or cleared. Every term below is open unless our own authority process confirms otherwise.

## 1. Material departures and pushback

### A. Liability architecture (most significant)

| Term | Seller draft | Our playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m (start). 20% only as conditional fallback with Amelia Frost's prior written authority naming the draft | Reject. The number matches our fallback, but no authority has been given, so it cannot be treated as cleared. Hold at 25% / AUD 6m. |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Five times our figure, and it would exclude many small claims entirely. |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, recoverable only above the basket | AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded | Reject. Under the Seller's structure we would absorb the first AUD 250,000 of losses. Ours is AUD 50,000 from the first dollar. |
| General claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only as fallback with Amelia Frost's written approval, none given) | Reject. Hold at 24 months. |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject outright. This would strip title and capacity protection, which is the core of what we are buying. |
| Cross-regime override | "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Reject. It turns a default rule into a way of pulling every category into the general regime. |

**Reasoning:** The combined effect is that the Seller would cap general claims at AUD 4.8m, require AUD 250,000 of losses before recovery starts, and apply the same limits to title. Individually each point is a departure. Together they make the warranty package largely illusory for a AUD 24m debt-free/cash-free deal.

### B. Fraud, reliance and exclusive remedy

- **Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Pushback:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is a non-waivable buyer position under the playbook. It should not be presented as a negotiable trade.

### C. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

- **Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2:** The Seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the whole data room as at 5pm 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Cl 8.3:** The Buyer has no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge of," including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Pushback:**
  - Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. Require specific, fair disclosure.
  - Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry.
  - Knowledge must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Reasoning:** Under §1.1, anything anywhere in the 2026 data room becomes disclosed against every warranty, which is effectively a sweeping disclosure against the whole warranty package. Combined with cl 8.3, the Seller would be able to argue we knew of and therefore cannot claim for matters they never specifically disclosed.

### D. Specific transaction issues

**Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% FY26 revenue, change-control consent cl 11.2/11.3)**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; treat consent as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." The Disclosure Letter confirms no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions is in the data room.
- Playbook: effective consent AND evidence that conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Pushback:** Make effective consent with satisfied conditions a condition precedent. Delete "treat as satisfied on delivery." A 30% revenue customer should not be left to endeavours.

**Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m outstanding, cl 8.1 change control, cl 9.2 discharge)**
- Seller: release "to be provided following Completion." The Disclosure Letter confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included.
- Playbook: current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Pushback:** Require a payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases delivered at Completion. The Seller's funds flow does not show an explicit Riverlark payout, so that also needs to be added. A post-Completion release is not acceptable without the required undertaking and approval.

**Ironquay IP (cl 11.1, DD-004 cl 7.3, DD-010 AUD 180,000)**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, "considered adequate." Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee. The AUD 180,000 open figure is not bank verification either way.
- Playbook: broaden the narrow indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as verified.
- **Pushback:** Broaden the indemnity to cover IP ownership and transfer defects generally, not just the SOW3 payment. Keep the cure mechanism. Require a payment receipt or confirmatory assignment, and independent verification of the AUD 180,000 position.

**Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000 plus on-costs)**
- Seller: "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in the funds flow. The disclosure does not say whether payroll tax or superannuation applies.
- Playbook: must be a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Pushback:** Add a specific line item for the AUD 420,000 and quantify the on-costs (payroll tax and superannuation) as a specific seller-funded deduction. Confirm whether the bonuses are conditional on Completion or continued employment, and how that affects the amount that will actually be payable.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006, ~1,240 records, Disclosure Letter §6)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- Disclosure Letter: no confirmed breach, unclear access, scope not established, notification requirement unknown, no loss amount stated.
- Playbook: assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Preserve logs, investigate, require updates.
- **Pushback:** Reject the materiality characterisation as unsupported. Require log preservation, an investigation timetable and regular written updates. Require a specific indemnity or escrow-style protection for losses arising from the incident. Obtain privacy counsel advice on whether any notification obligation could arise. I'm not reaching that conclusion here, but the personal data involved (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) means it should be assessed, not assumed away.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate)**
- Seller: "ordinary-course operating costs." The Disclosure Letter says the material does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. The Seller's own description conflicts with its disclosure.
- Playbook: assess. No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
- **Pushback:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label. Require contract copies and an assessment of whether any amounts are accrued or are effectively debt-like. Any treatment as debt or a price adjustment should be a separate negotiated point, not an automatic one.

**Title (DD-012)**
- Seller: title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."
- Playbook: DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof of title, encumbrances or authority.
- **Pushback:** Require independent evidence: ASIC company extract, a verified chain of transfers, PPSR and other encumbrance searches, and evidence of corporate authority. The Seller's disclosure itself says the Buyer has not completed its own verification.

**Tax and IP**
- Seller: "settled under the general regime."
- Playbook: these terms remain open and do not have unlimited liability or resolution assumed.
- **Pushback:** Reject. Tax and IP need their own regimes and remain open for negotiation.

**Other disclosure items**
- **Office lease (§7):** Confirm whether landlord consent is required for the share sale. The disclosure only mentions a notification obligation.
- **Mossvale (§9):** Confirm whether an assignment restriction is triggered by a share sale. Disclosure does not say it is.
- **Disclosure Letter §1.4 (non-admission):** Acceptable as a general reservation, but it should not be read as qualifying specific warranties.

## 2. Recommendations summary

1. **Hold the playbook position on caps:** 25% / AUD 6m general cap. Do not accept AUD 4.8m or 18 months without Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the specific draft.
2. **Reset thresholds:** AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket.
3. **Separate Fundamental/Title:** 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside general limits. Delete the cross-regime override.
4. **Carve out fraud:** From all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable.
5. **Disclosure:** Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
6. **Buyer knowledge:** Delete cl 8.3. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** Effective consent and satisfied conditions as a Completion condition. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours.
8. **Riverlark:** Payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
9. **Bonuses:** Specific funds-flow line item for AUD 420,000 plus quantified on-costs, or seller-funded.
10. **Ironquay:** Broaden the indemnity, keep the SOW3 cure, and verify the AUD 180,000 independently.
11. **DD-006:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates, obtain privacy advice, and seek specific protection. Make no materiality or breach assumption either way.
12. **Sandbar:** Assess the contracts. No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
13. **Title:** Require independent ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is not sufficient.
14. **Tax and IP:** Keep open and separate. Do not accept the Seller's "settled" characterisation.
15. **Verify cross-references:** The clause numbers in the Seller summary (cl 2/3/6/7/8/9/11/12/13/20) appear inconsistent with each other. Check them against the full draft before marking up.

**Immediate actions:** Obtain Amelia Frost's position on whether any fallback should be considered at all. Start independent title and encumbrance searches. Obtain bank confirmation for the Ironquay position and a Riverlark payout letter. Request the full SPA draft so the summary positions can be checked against the operative clauses.
=== END ADVICE ===
